summary: Johannes Schubert worked in Tibetology and Sinology. He studied at Leipzig and Humboldt University of Berlin under mentors including August Conrady and Erich Haenisch. He served at the Leipzig University Library (1928–1954) and held professorial and directorial posts at Leipzig (1934–1965).

Johannes Toepffer was a scholar in history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Tartu under Leo Meyer (~1878–1882) and under Ulrich von Wilamowitz-Moellendorff (~1883–1885). He held a post at the University of Basel (~1894–1895).

John A. Ardussi specializes in Tibetology, history, and archaeology. He studied under MA supervisor Turrell V. Wylie and earned his PhD from Australian National University (attested 1977). His career includes positions at the CNRS, ELDEC Corporation, and the University of Virginia.

John Alexander Corrie Boswell was an Indologist and historian. He served as a colonial civil servant in the Madras Civil Service from 1855 to 1871 and in the Indian Civil Service from around 1856 to 1872.

John Alexander Jorgensen works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He completed an MA at Australian National University under Kenneth H. J. Gardiner, later holding posts there (attested 1982, 2014–2015) and serving as senior lecturer at Griffith University (attested 2012).

John Alexander Stewart was a scholar of linguistics who studied at the University of Aberdeen (~1899–1903). After serving in the Indian Civil Service (~1905–1933), he worked at SOAS (~1933–1948) and as Reader in Burmese at the University of London (~1933–1944).

John Allan worked in Indology, history, and archaeology after studying at the Universities of Edinburgh (~1901–1905) and Leipzig (~1905–1907). He worked at the British Museum (1907–1949) and lectured in Sanskrit at UCL (1907–1917), SOAS (1920–1922), and Edinburgh (1949–1955).

John Anderson was an MD graduate of the University of Edinburgh (~1857–1862) working in Indology, history, and archaeology. He was Professor of Natural History at Free Church College (~1862–1864), curator/supervisor at the Indian Museum, Kolkata (1865–1886), and professor at Calcutta Medical College (1877).
John Archibald Boyle was an Indologist who studied at Radley College from around 1857 to 1858. He served as a civil servant in the Madras Civil Service beginning in 1865.

John Avery was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Amherst, Yale under William Dwight Whitney, Berlin, and Tübingen. He served as a tutor at Amherst (1862) and as Professor of Greek at Grinnell College (1870–1877) and Bowdoin College (1877–1887).
John B. Carman is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He served as Director of the Center for the Study of World Religions and held a post at Harvard University (attested 1999).

John B. Cobb Jr. is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who earned his PhD at the University of Chicago. He founded the Center for Process Studies and held professorships at Claremont School of Theology and Claremont Graduate University (attested 1989).

John Beames was an Indologist and linguist educated at Merchant Taylors' School and East India Company College (Haileybury) between 1856 and 1857. He subsequently served in the Indian Civil Service from around 1858 to 1893.

John Borthwick Gilchrist worked in linguistics and Indology, earning an LL.D. from Edinburgh. He served in the East India Company, was principal of Fort William College (1800–1804), taught at East India Company College, and was Professor of Hindustani at UCL (~1828–1831).
John Bray is a scholar in Tibetology, history, and archaeology. He studied under Tsering Dhundup Gonkatsang and has held a post at the International Association for Ladakh Studies.
John Briggs was a scholar in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Eton College until 1799 and later served in the East India Company from around 1801 to 1835.

John Brockington is an Indologist who earned an MA and DPhil at Oxford. He held posts at the University of Edinburgh as Senior Lecturer (attested 1987) and Emeritus Professor of Sanskrit (attested 1997–2014), and served in the International Association of Sanskrit Studies.

John Brough was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Edinburgh under Arthur Berriedale Keith and Cambridge under Harold Walter Bailey. He held posts at the British Museum, SOAS/University of London (1946–1967), and served as Professor at Cambridge (1967–1984).

John Buescher is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his doctoral dissertation at the University of Virginia in 1982 and served as a Director at Voice of America (attested 2001).

John Burnet was a scholar of philosophy who studied at the Royal High School, the University of Edinburgh (~1879–1882), and Balliol College, Oxford (~1883–1887). He held a post at the University of St Andrews from around 1892 to 1926.
